title: Executor cancel of a resting order on tradeify_1 (text-less icon cancel control)
note: Manager Session 2026-10-08 (session_01Uq7MrjPQDRWqbhCjwuMava) dispatch; operator ~16:22Z 'the system needs to be a fully autonomous pipeline'. Ticket prop-manual-e6badec7ae10 (LIMIT sell ETHUSD 0.82 @ 2471.31, valid_until 16:26:53Z) rested past expiry: the expiry cancel failed 'rows=1, controls=0'. MEASURED (system-action run 37810774267, issue #17157, 16:42Z): the orders row's cancel is a text-less <button class='button button-icon grid-orders_control'> drawing <use xlink:href='#icon-close-order'>, beside a modify button drawing '#icon-replace-context'. FIX: ROW_ACTION_JS also matches an ANCHORED icon reference (^#?icon-(close|cancel)-order$) inside a pressable only, still exactly 1 row by Order ID and exactly 1 control; the row is hovered and re-read first. Executor: an exhausted expiry cancel keeps trying the guarded cancel quietly every cycle (alerts stay hourly), so a fixed matcher cancels it without a human. CLOSES WHEN: the journal of ict-prop-executor@tradeify_1 shows a cancel_expired_resting result clicked=true for the stale order, then orders 0 and the ticket reported skipped/expired. [!] ROUND 1 MERGED (#17158, 18:05Z) AND DEPLOYED, NOT YET EFFECTIVE. OBSERVED in the ict-prop-executor@tradeify_1 journal: cycles at 18:13Z and 18:18Z ran code_sha 179e4d551, located the ONE #icon-close-order control on order 18912998 and clicked it (ok=true, clicked=true, why 'clicked', no role=dialog left open), yet every following read shows orders 1. So the matcher half works; the click does not cancel. ROUND 2 (this PR): the click's PRODUCT is captured (new buttons, the overlay holding them, whether the row is still there) into the action's why, and a confirmation is pressed ONLY when the overlay says 'cancel' and exactly one new enabled button is an anchored confirm label (confirm|ok|yes|yes, cancel|cancel order|yes, cancel order). The exhausted-retry path re-clicks every 5 min, so the first cycle on round-2 code either cancels or names what the terminal showed.
